signature.name: Budva Old Town
signature.detail: Budva's walled old town sits on the Adriatic and is the city's historic heart, with narrow stone streets, churches and sea walls to walk along. Go in the early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday crowds and heat in summer.

signature.name: Sveti Stefan
signature.detail: This former fishing village on a small islet joined to the mainland by a causeway is one of Montenegro's best-known views. It is mostly seen from outside, as access to the islet is restricted, so plan your visit around the viewpoints on the road.

signature.name: Sveti Stefan Beach
signature.detail: This beach lies in front of the Sveti Stefan islet and is popular for swimming and sunbathing with a view of the village. Arrive early in peak summer for a good spot, and bring water shoes for the pebbly shoreline.

signature.name: Kotor Old Town
signature.detail: Kotor's medieval walled town sits at the head of the Bay of Kotor and is a UNESCO-listed highlight within easy reach of Budva. Wear comfortable shoes, since the route up the city walls is steep, and visit mid-morning or after 4 pm when cruise groups are fewer.

signature.name: Perast
signature.detail: Perast is a small town of Venetian-era palaces on the Bay of Kotor, famous for its waterfront and the islets offshore. It is best reached by bus or tour, and an unhurried lunch on the promenade makes a good half-day stop.

signature.name: Bay of Kotor Cruise
signature.detail: A boat trip across the Bay of Kotor shows the mountains, towns and islands from the water, which is hard to see any other way. Book a morning departure for calmer water and clearer views, and check whether the cruise includes swimming stops.

signature.name: Skadar Lake National Park
signature.detail: This large lake on the Montenegro-Albania border is a protected wetland known for birdlife, water lilies and small islands. Boat tours leave from Virpazar and are the best way to explore, so book ahead in summer.

signature.name: Mausoleum of Njegoš on Lovćen
signature.detail: The mausoleum of the poet-prince Njegoš stands on Mount Lovćen above the Bay of Kotor, with wide views over the coast. The road up has many hairpin bends, so a guided tour or taxi is easier than driving yourself in poor weather.

food: Casual meal $10-18; seafood restaurants on the old town squares run $20-35
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $90-150 a night in summer; cheaper outside peak season
transport: Local buses about $1-2 a ride; taxis $3-6 for short trips; car hire is useful for the coast
